reason: This passage from Exodus 16 (the manna narrative) emphasizes God's provision, obedience to commandments (מִצְוֺתַי וְתוֹרֹתָֽי), and observance of the Sabbath rest. The text does not address worship practices or sacrifices. God's concern in this passage is whether the people will follow His law (תוֹרָתִי) through the daily test of manna collection and Sabbath observance. While Sabbath rest could be understood as a form of worship, the statement specifically invokes 'proper worship and sacrifice,' and this text contains no mention of sacrifices or formal worship practices whatsoever.
